title: Your First Day at the Community Print Studio
transcript:
Welcome to the community print studio. Before you choose a workspace, I want to explain how the building operates. We share it with a youth photography group, so some rooms that look empty may be reserved for their sessions. Today's induction covers the printing area; it does not give access to the photography equipment.

Please put bags and coats in the lockers beside the entrance. The small keys have numbered wooden tags, and you keep your key until you leave. Clear floors are particularly important here because people often carry large sheets of paper that block their view of what is under their feet.

The presses are arranged along the far wall. Before using one, sign the register on the shelf beside it. This records who is working with each press and makes it easier to contact the right person if equipment needs checking. It is not a booking system. Reservations for busy periods are made online, and unused bookings are released after fifteen minutes.

There is a drying rack near the windows. Put your name and the date on a slip underneath your work, rather than writing on the print itself. Pieces left for more than a week will be moved into the collection cupboard. We will contact you before disposing of anything, but please do not treat the studio as permanent storage.

You may bring your own materials, though they must be approved before use. Some products sold for home crafts can damage our rollers or require ventilation that this building cannot provide. Ask the supervisor before opening an unfamiliar container. You should also tell us about any spills immediately, even if you think you have already cleaned them up.

The membership fee includes ordinary paper for practice. Specialist paper is charged separately, and you pay only for the sheets you take. We keep small sample books so you can compare surfaces before buying a whole pack elsewhere.

Finally, this evening's demonstration will focus on how pressure changes a printed image. The visiting artist will make several versions from the same plate. You are welcome to watch without booking, but practical places are limited to people who have completed this induction. If you only want to observe, please stand behind the marked line so the working area stays clear.

options: They may be unsuitable for the equipment or building
They are always more expensive than studio supplies
The studio sells all materials used by members
